snip.t: Acute chest syndrome: Young children present with chest pain, fever, cough, tachypnea, leukocytosis, and pulmonary infiltrates in the upper lobes; adults are usually afebrile, dyspneic with severe chest pain, with multilobar/lower lobe disease
Acute chest syndrome needs a cephalosporin plus a macrolide to cover typical and atypical organisms.

snip.t: Sickle Cell Disease: Can present with acute chest syndrome, which may involve pericardial inflammation or effusion.
Obstructive: Extracardiac flow obstruction — Pericardial tamponade (TB pericarditis), tension pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, sickle cell acute chest syndrome
Sickle Cell Disease: Precipitates hypovolemic shock (splenic sequestration crisis in children) or obstructive shock (acute chest syndrome with cor pulmonale).
Chest findings (crepitations, tachypnoea): Acute chest syndrome – pulmonary vaso‑occlusion, infection, or fat embolism.
